# Swiss signage design

The earlier detailed design discussion was not recoverable from the available chat history. This brief records the explicit direction and subsequent owner corrections for this project.

- Use Swiss transport signage as the visual reference: strict alignment, modular grids, numbered sections, clear hierarchy, flat surfaces and strong rules between comparison rows.
- Helvetica/Arial or an equivalent neutral grotesque. Large, tightly composed headings; tabular numerals for ILS totals; comfortable text sizes for conditions and timestamps. Use local/system fonts initially.
- Paper/white backgrounds and near-black type form the neutral structure. Color never decorates an arbitrary heading or vendor.
- Green means verified in-stock availability. Red means out of stock/unavailable. Amber/yellow means pending, uncertain or stale. Always write the status as text; color alone is insufficient. “Best delivered total” should be stated explicitly without a second ambiguous green meaning.
- No emoji in typography. Arrows and wayfinding marks must be monochrome SVG or unambiguous text glyphs that cannot render as colorful emoji. No flags, shopping-cart emoji, coffee emoji or emoji badges.
- Clear rows with consistent columns: vendor, pack/quantity, item price, shipping, delivered total, stock and checked time. At narrow widths reflow each row while preserving the same hierarchy; do not hide shipping conditions.
- Buttons and links require visible keyboard focus. Aim for WCAG AA contrast. Support RTL fragments and Hebrew vendor/product text with correct directionality.
- Prefer factual shopping copy. Distinguish checked data, inferred estimates, stale observations and unknowns. Avoid fake success counters and invented prices.

# Architecture and authority

There are two independent loops:

1. Shurik on GitHub Actions develops and checkpoints source to main. It uses only OPENCODE_API_KEY and the repository GITHUB_TOKEN. Its state/history is public on shurik-control/main.
2. The deployed Worker refreshes vendor observations using deterministic scheduled adapters, persists them through runtime bindings and serves the public comparison board. It does not need Shurik or an LLM to keep refreshing.

Cloudflare Workers Builds will be connected by the owner after the second handoff. It observes main pushes and performs validation before deploying. No CF deployment workflow or CF API secret belongs in GitHub. Exclude shurik-control/* and all other branches from Cloudflare builds and previews.

This prevents Shurik's Actions process from directly authenticating to CF. It is not a sandbox for agent-authored code: Shurik writes main, so its code and configuration can influence the CF build and live Worker. CF build commands can run source-controlled code in a credentialed environment. Restrict the CF build token to this Worker and the minimum required permissions; avoid broad account permissions or unrelated build/runtime secrets. Prefer runtime bindings over administrative API tokens. Never give the public Worker an administrative CF token.

GitHub normally does not trigger another push workflow for a push using GITHUB_TOKEN. Do not rely on CI being automatically triggered by every Shurik checkpoint. Shurik must run local verification, and Cloudflare's build command must run npm run verify for every deployment. After connecting CF, verify one actual Shurik push reaches Workers Builds; never assume third-party webhook behavior from GitHub Actions behavior alone.

Start with vendor-specific adapters, a shared product/offer schema, a pure quote/ranking module, persistence and the scheduled-handler pipeline. Keep fetching separate from parsing and pricing. Fixture tests should cover unstable vendor HTML and quote edge cases. Store observation timestamps independently from refresh-attempt timestamps. Public routes are read-only and use cached snapshots; public shoppers must not be able to initiate unlimited vendor traffic.

Initial scaffold: static assets plus /health and /api/catalog. No real offers, storage or cron are implemented yet. The target product exists, but prices and availability remain explicitly unknown. The coding agent is responsible for building and proving the runtime described in PROMPT.md.

content.text:
# Attention shoppers. Happy hunting.

Build a public, self-updating website on Cloudflare Workers that finds ways to order products online for delivery in Israel and compares the item price plus shipping. Start with Lavazza Crema e Gusto vacuum-packed ground coffee, then make it straightforward to add other products and vendors. This is a working shopping tool, not a marketing landing page.

The owner chose Shurik v1, opencode-go/step-5-preview-free at its maximum supported reasoning, high. Assume capability comparable to DeepSeek V4.1 Flash when organizing work: use concrete milestones, short feedback cycles and verifiable evidence. Do not change provider/model or switch to a paid model. If the free model becomes unavailable, record the issue for the maintainer.

The coding loop writes directly to main. After the owner connects Cloudflare Workers Builds, main pushes will auto-deploy. Shurik has no Cloudflare credentials, API access or deployment tools. All development and integration validation must work locally. Read AGENTS.md and the design/architecture docs.

## Required shopping behavior

1. Discover and validate several actual vendor listings. Use public vendor APIs or public product pages and permitted structured data. Record source URLs, retrieval dates and what each source establishes. Prefer vendors serving Israel; international vendors qualify only when delivery to Israel is evidenced.
2. Match the actual product: Lavazza, Crema e Gusto, ground coffee in a vacuum brick. Record grams, pack count and blend variant. Do not confuse beans, capsules, pods or similarly named products. Classico, Forte and other variants must remain separate. A typical 250 g pack is a starting hypothesis, not a verified fact for every listing.
3. Let shoppers choose a sensible quantity and Israeli delivery locality/postcode. Do not collect or store a street address. Different pack sizes and multipacks should normalize to delivered ILS per kilogram and the actual checkout total. Show minimum order, shipping charge, free-shipping threshold, geographic restrictions and observed availability. Keep pickup separate from delivery.
4. Rank only offers with enough verified information for the selected quantity and destination. Item price + shipping + mandatory fees is the comparison total. Unknown shipping, import charges or FX conversion must not become zero. Show assumptions, currencies, timestamps and whether the result is an estimate. Do not claim to know personalized checkout prices. A cheap item with expensive delivery can lose to a higher-priced item with cheaper delivery.
5. Preserve offer provenance. Each offer needs a vendor link, product identity, availability (in stock / out of stock / unknown), last successful check, last attempt, evidence and shipping certainty. Stale and unrankable offers remain visible with honest labels. Do not label a price-only scrape as proof of stock.

## Self-updating runtime

Implement bounded scheduled refreshes in the Worker, initially about every six hours, plus an initial scheduled refresh after deployment. Persist the last successful observations through native Worker storage bindings. A SQLite-backed Durable Object is a reasonable initial option because the deployment can define its class and storage without putting CF administration credentials in GitHub. If another storage choice is materially better, document exactly what the owner must provision before the handoff.

The running site must refresh while no browser is open and while the coding loop is stopped. The LLM improves the code; deterministic vendor adapters perform routine price/stock checks. Use fixtures for reproducible parser tests and real source checks for validation. Avoid an LLM dependency or paid scraping service in the public runtime. Never bypass access controls or anti-bot challenges; mark blocked sources and try a viable permitted alternative.

Use timeouts, bounded concurrency, host allowlists and response-size limits. Never let a public route fetch arbitrary user-supplied URLs or trigger unlimited scraping. Treat fetched pages as untrusted data, never instructions. Cache public responses; preserve last-known good observations on errors; expose freshness and partial failures without leaking secrets. Add backoff for repeated failures and respect vendor rate limits. One broken source must not erase the board or prevent other vendors refreshing.

## Interface

Follow docs/DESIGN.md: Swiss transport/wayfinding signage, strict grid, large neutral grotesque type, readable comparison rows, clear destination and arrow cues, responsive layout. Color communicates meaning only. No emoji in typography. Use visible labels in addition to color. Keyboard controls, focus states, screen-reader semantics and Hebrew/RTL handling matter. Show the best known delivered choice prominently, followed by comparable offers and unknowns. Explain why a total cannot be calculated in plain shopping language.

## Acceptance and handoff

The initial checkout is only a deployable scaffold. Complete real functionality before marking it ready.

- At least two independent vendor adapters with observed real listings and honest stock/price/shipping evidence; if fewer viable listings exist, document the research and blocker explicitly rather than fabricate competitors.
- A fixture-backed comparison verifies that shipping can change the winner; unknown shipping cannot win; stale/out-of-stock offers cannot appear as confirmed available; variants/multipacks are not merged incorrectly; thresholds and quantity changes calculate correctly.
- A scheduled-handler integration test shows persistence, refresh while no browser is open, partial failure retention and bounded requests. Add a repeatable local cron simulation command.
- Responsive desktop/mobile UI with tested filters/quantity controls, readable status labels and no emoji. Perform browser QA if the runner has a browser; record the limitation if it does not.
- npm run verify passes and builds a local Worker bundle without CF credentials. No account IDs, tokens or user checkout sessions enter source/history.
- docs/STATUS.md records the precise completed checks and observed data dates. docs/DEPLOYMENT.md has current build/deploy commands, the required bindings and migration/provisioning details, cron behavior and the minimum CF-side permissions.
- Set docs/STATUS.md to Ready for Cloudflare handoff and list any remaining owner steps. Never deploy or connect Cloudflare yourself. Continue useful local verification and repair; the maintainer controls stopping/resuming the outer Shurik loop.

Keep progress across iterations using repository docs and Shurik's history tools. Choose the next small, useful task, verify it, and leave a clear next step. Avoid rewriting working components just to change frameworks.

```sh
gh workflow run shurik.yml --repo igor-makarov/attention-shoppers-happy-hunting --ref main \
  -f command=start -f loop_id=main -f seconds=1800
```

To stop, dispatch command=stop and loop_id=main. Record the durable stop before turning SHURIK_ENABLED false. To resume, use command=resume, loop_id=main; the workflow supplies high reasoning again. Control/session history and Actions logs are public; do not add private material to this task.

# Attention shoppers. Happy hunting.

Build a public, self-updating website on Cloudflare Workers that finds ways to order products online for delivery in Israel and compares the item price plus shipping. Start with Lavazza Crema e Gusto vacuum-packed ground coffee, then make it straightforward to add other products and vendors. This is a working shopping tool, not a marketing landing page.

The owner chose Shurik v1 and explicitly switched the coding loop to opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash at its maximum supported reasoning, max, after repeated Step 5 endpoint errors. Use concrete milestones, short feedback cycles and verifiable evidence. This specific model switch is authorized; do not change provider/model or add another fallback without the owner's instruction. If the provider becomes unavailable, record the issue for the maintainer.

The coding loop writes directly to main. After the owner connects Cloudflare Workers Builds, main pushes will auto-deploy. Shurik has no Cloudflare credentials, API access or deployment tools. All development and integration validation must work locally. Read AGENTS.md and the design/architecture docs.

## Required shopping behavior

1. Discover and validate several actual vendor listings. Use public vendor APIs or public product pages and permitted structured data. Record source URLs, retrieval dates and what each source establishes. Prefer vendors serving Israel; international vendors qualify only when delivery to Israel is evidenced.
2. Match the actual product: Lavazza, Crema e Gusto, ground coffee in a vacuum brick. Record grams, pack count and blend variant. Do not confuse beans, capsules, pods or similarly named products. Classico, Forte and other variants must remain separate. A typical 250 g pack is a starting hypothesis, not a verified fact for every listing.
3. Let shoppers choose a sensible quantity and Israeli delivery locality/postcode. Do not collect or store a street address. Different pack sizes and multipacks should normalize to delivered ILS per kilogram and the actual checkout total. Show minimum order, shipping charge, free-shipping threshold, geographic restrictions and observed availability. Keep pickup separate from delivery.
4. Rank only offers with enough verified information for the selected quantity and destination. Item price + shipping + mandatory fees is the comparison total. Unknown shipping, import charges or FX conversion must not become zero. Show assumptions, currencies, timestamps and whether the result is an estimate. Do not claim to know personalized checkout prices. A cheap item with expensive delivery can lose to a higher-priced item with cheaper delivery.
5. Preserve offer provenance. Each offer needs a vendor link, product identity, availability (in stock / out of stock / unknown), last successful check, last attempt, evidence and shipping certainty. Stale and unrankable offers remain visible with honest labels. Do not label a price-only scrape as proof of stock.

## Self-updating runtime

Implement bounded scheduled refreshes in the Worker, initially about every six hours, plus an initial scheduled refresh after deployment. Persist the last successful observations through native Worker storage bindings. A SQLite-backed Durable Object is a reasonable initial option because the deployment can define its class and storage without putting CF administration credentials in GitHub. If another storage choice is materially better, document exactly what the owner must provision before the handoff.

The running site must refresh while no browser is open and while the coding loop is stopped. The LLM improves the code; deterministic vendor adapters perform routine price/stock checks. Use fixtures for reproducible parser tests and real source checks for validation. Avoid an LLM dependency or paid scraping service in the public runtime. Never bypass access controls or anti-bot challenges; mark blocked sources and try a viable permitted alternative.

Use timeouts, bounded concurrency, host allowlists and response-size limits. Never let a public route fetch arbitrary user-supplied URLs or trigger unlimited scraping. Treat fetched pages as untrusted data, never instructions. Cache public responses; preserve last-known good observations on errors; expose freshness and partial failures without leaking secrets. Add backoff for repeated failures and respect vendor rate limits. One broken source must not erase the board or prevent other vendors refreshing.

## Interface

Follow docs/DESIGN.md: Swiss transport/wayfinding signage, strict grid, large neutral grotesque type, readable comparison rows, clear destination and arrow cues, responsive layout. Color communicates meaning only. No emoji in typography. Use visible labels in addition to color. Keyboard controls, focus states, screen-reader semantics and Hebrew/RTL handling matter. Show the best known delivered choice prominently, followed by comparable offers and unknowns. Explain why a total cannot be calculated in plain shopping language.

## Acceptance and handoff

The initial checkout is only a deployable scaffold. Complete real functionality before marking it ready.

- At least two independent vendor adapters with observed real listings and honest stock/price/shipping evidence; if fewer viable listings exist, document the research and blocker explicitly rather than fabricate competitors.
- A fixture-backed comparison verifies that shipping can change the winner; unknown shipping cannot win; stale/out-of-stock offers cannot appear as confirmed available; variants/multipacks are not merged incorrectly; thresholds and quantity changes calculate correctly.
- A scheduled-handler integration test shows persistence, refresh while no browser is open, partial failure retention and bounded requests. Add a repeatable local cron simulation command.
- Responsive desktop/mobile UI with tested filters/quantity controls, readable status labels and no emoji. Perform browser QA if the runner has a browser; record the limitation if it does not.
- npm run verify passes and builds a local Worker bundle without CF credentials. No account IDs, tokens or user checkout sessions enter source/history.
- docs/STATUS.md records the precise completed checks and observed data dates. docs/DEPLOYMENT.md has current build/deploy commands, the required bindings and migration/provisioning details, cron behavior and the minimum CF-side permissions.
- Set docs/STATUS.md to Ready for Cloudflare handoff and list any remaining owner steps. Never deploy or connect Cloudflare yourself. Continue useful local verification and repair; the maintainer controls stopping/resuming the outer Shurik loop.

Keep progress across iterations using repository docs and Shurik's history tools. Choose the next small, useful task, verify it, and leave a clear next step. Avoid rewriting working components just to change frameworks.

Read PROMPT.md, docs/DESIGN.md, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md and docs/STATUS.md before work.

- Work directly on main, as authorized by the owner. Keep each checkpoint useful and testable. Do not change Shurik's control branch or engine.

- Never invent stock, product identity, prices, shipping, delivery times or successful refreshes. Publish evidence and timestamps; preserve unknowns and previous good data on errors.
- Colors must convey status or meaning. No emoji in the website typography. Use labels and monochrome vector wayfinding symbols.
- Run npm run verify before completing each change. Keep dependencies pinned and package-lock.json current.

====PROMPT====
# Attention shoppers. Happy hunting.

Build a public, self-updating website on Cloudflare Workers that finds ways to order products online for delivery in Israel and compares the item price plus shipping. Start with Lavazza Crema e Gusto vacuum-packed ground coffee, then make it straightforward to add other products and vendors. This is a working shopping tool, not a marketing landing page.

The owner chose Shurik v1 and explicitly switched the coding loop to opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash at its maximum supported reasoning, max, after repeated Step 5 endpoint errors. Use concrete milestones, short feedback cycles and verifiable evidence. This specific model switch is authorized; do not change provider/model or add another fallback without the owner's instruction. If the provider becomes unavailable, record the issue for the maintainer.

The coding loop writes directly to main. After the owner connects Cloudflare Workers Builds, main pushes will auto-deploy. Shurik has no Cloudflare credentials, API access or deployment tools. All development and integration validation must work locally. Read AGENTS.md and the design/architecture docs.

## Required shopping behavior

1. Discover and validate several actual vendor listings. Use public vendor APIs or public product pages and permitted structured data. Record source URLs, retrieval dates and what each source establishes. Prefer vendors serving Israel; international vendors qualify only when delivery to Israel is evidenced.
2. Match the actual product: Lavazza, Crema e Gusto, ground coffee in a vacuum brick. Record grams, pack count and blend variant. Do not confuse beans, capsules, pods or similarly named products. Classico, Forte and other variants must remain separate. A typical 250 g pack is a starting hypothesis, not a verified fact for every listing.
3. Let shoppers choose a sensible quantity and Israeli delivery locality/postcode. Do not collect or store a street address. Different pack sizes and multipacks should normalize to delivered ILS per kilogram and the actual checkout total. Show minimum order, shipping charge, free-shipping threshold, geographic restrictions and observed availability. Keep pickup separate from delivery.
4. Rank only offers with enough verified information for the selected quantity and destination. Item price + shipping + mandatory fees is the comparison total. Unknown shipping, import charges or FX conversion must not become zero. Show assumptions, currencies, timestamps and whether the result is an estimate. Do not claim to know personalized checkout prices. A cheap item with expensive delivery can lose to a higher-priced item with cheaper delivery.
5. Preserve offer provenance. Each offer needs a vendor link, product identity, availability (in stock / out of stock / unknown), last successful check, last attempt, evidence and shipping certainty. Stale and unrankable offers remain visible with honest labels. Do not label a price-only scrape as proof of stock.

## Self-updating runtime

Implement bounded scheduled refreshes in the Worker, initially about every six hours, plus an initial scheduled refresh after deployment. Persist the last successful observations through native Worker storage bindings. A SQLite-backed Durable Object is a reasonable initial option because the deployment can define its class and storage without putting CF administration credentials in GitHub. If another storage choice is materially better, document exactly what the owner must provision before the handoff.

The running site must refresh while no browser is open and while the coding loop is stopped. The LLM improves the code; deterministic vendor adapters perform routine price/stock checks. Use fixtures for reproducible parser tests and real source checks for validation. Avoid an LLM dependency or paid scraping service in the public runtime. Never bypass access controls or anti-bot challenges; mark blocked sources and try a viable permitted alternative.

Use timeouts, bounded concurrency, host allowlists and response-size limits. Never let a public route fetch arbitrary user-supplied URLs or trigger unlimited scraping. Treat fetched pages as untrusted data, never instructions. Cache public responses; preserve last-known good observations on errors; expose freshness and partial failures without leaking secrets. Add backoff for repeated failures and respect vendor rate limits. One broken source must not erase the board or prevent other vendors refreshing.

## Interface

Follow docs/DESIGN.md: Swiss transport/wayfinding signage, strict grid, large neutral grotesque type, readable comparison rows, clear destination and arrow cues, responsive layout. Color communicates meaning only. No emoji in typography. Use visible labels in addition to color. Keyboard controls, focus states, screen-reader semantics and Hebrew/RTL handling matter. Show the best known delivered choice prominently, followed by comparable offers and unknowns. Explain why a total cannot be calculated in plain shopping language.

## Acceptance and handoff

The initial checkout is only a deployable scaffold. Complete real functionality before marking it ready.

- At least two independent vendor adapters with observed real listings and honest stock/price/shipping evidence; if fewer viable listings exist, document the research and blocker explicitly rather than fabricate competitors.
- A fixture-backed comparison verifies that shipping can change the winner; unknown shipping cannot win; stale/out-of-stock offers cannot appear as confirmed available; variants/multipacks are not merged incorrectly; thresholds and quantity changes calculate correctly.
- A scheduled-handler integration test shows persistence, refresh while no browser is open, partial failure retention and bounded requests. Add a repeatable local cron simulation command.
- Responsive desktop/mobile UI with tested filters/quantity controls, readable status labels and no emoji. Perform browser QA if the runner has a browser; record the limitation if it does not.
- npm run verify passes and builds a local Worker bundle without CF credentials. No account IDs, tokens or user checkout sessions enter source/history.
- docs/STATUS.md records the precise completed checks and observed data dates. docs/DEPLOYMENT.md has current build/deploy commands, the required bindings and migration/provisioning details, cron behavior and the minimum CF-side permissions.
- Set docs/STATUS.md to Ready for Cloudflare handoff and list any remaining owner steps. Never deploy or connect Cloudflare yourself. Continue useful local verification and repair; the maintainer controls stopping/resuming the outer Shurik loop.

Keep progress across iterations using repository docs and Shurik's history tools. Choose the next small, useful task, verify it, and leave a clear next step. Avoid rewriting working components just to change frameworks.
====README====
# Attention shoppers. Happy hunting.

A public online shopping board for delivery in Israel, starting with **Lavazza Crema e Gusto vacuum-packed ground coffee**. The goal is to compare actual availability and item price plus shipping for a selected quantity and destination, with visible source evidence and freshness.

Swiss signage design, meaningful status colors, no emoji typography. Unknown shipping is never silently treated as free.

This initial commit is a deployable scaffold, not a completed price tracker. Shurik builds the remaining functionality from [PROMPT.md](PROMPT.md). See [current status](docs/STATUS.md), [design](docs/DESIGN.md) and [architecture](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md).

## Coding loop

The workflow uses [igor-makarov/shurik@v1](https://github.com/igor-makarov/shurik), opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash and max reasoning. The owner chose direct work on main and has added the OPENCODE_API_KEY Actions secret. The first handoff is complete; the main loop will develop the tracker while Cloudflare remains disconnected. Check the Actions page and shurik-control/main for live loop state.

DeepSeek V4.1 Flash is present in Shurik's pinned Pi AI catalog and supports low, high and max reasoning. Its native adapter preserves reasoning content across tool calls. The owner authorized this switch after Step 5 returned repeated unavailable-endpoint errors. No further model fallback is permitted without an owner instruction.

## Deployment and refreshing

The owner will enable auto-deploy on main pushes from **Cloudflare Workers Builds** at the second handoff. GitHub stores no CF credentials and has no deployment job. Once implemented, Worker Cron Triggers and native runtime storage will refresh the offer board independently of the coding loop.

Follow [the two handoffs](docs/DEPLOYMENT.md). Agent-authored code can affect the CF build and production Worker once auto-deploy is enabled; keeping CF API credentials out of Shurik does not remove that authority.

## Develop locally

```sh
npm run verify
npm run dev
```

The verification build is Wrangler deploy --dry-run and does not publish to Cloudflare.

# Architecture and authority

There are two independent loops:

1. Shurik on GitHub Actions develops and checkpoints source to main. It uses only OPENCODE_API_KEY and the repository GITHUB_TOKEN. Its state/history is public on shurik-control/main.
2. The deployed Worker refreshes vendor observations using deterministic scheduled adapters, persists them through runtime bindings and serves the public comparison board. It does not need Shurik or an LLM to keep refreshing.

Cloudflare Workers Builds will be connected by the owner after the second handoff. It observes main pushes and performs validation before deploying. No CF deployment workflow or CF API secret belongs in GitHub. Exclude shurik-control/* and all other branches from Cloudflare builds and previews.

This prevents Shurik's Actions process from directly authenticating to CF. It is not a sandbox for agent-authored code: Shurik writes main, so its code and configuration can influence the CF build and live Worker. CF build commands can run source-controlled code in a credentialed environment. Restrict the CF build token to this Worker and the minimum required permissions; avoid broad account permissions or unrelated build/runtime secrets. Prefer runtime bindings over administrative API tokens. Never give the public Worker an administrative CF token.

GitHub normally does not trigger another push workflow for a push using GITHUB_TOKEN. Do not rely on CI being automatically triggered by every Shurik checkpoint. Shurik must run local verification, and Cloudflare's build command must run npm run verify for every deployment. After connecting CF, verify one actual Shurik push reaches Workers Builds; never assume third-party webhook behavior from GitHub Actions behavior alone.

Start with vendor-specific adapters, a shared product/offer schema, a pure quote/ranking module, persistence and the scheduled-handler pipeline. Keep fetching separate from parsing and pricing. Fixture tests should cover unstable vendor HTML and quote edge cases. Store observation timestamps independently from refresh-attempt timestamps. Public routes are read-only and use cached snapshots; public shoppers must not be able to initiate unlimited vendor traffic.

Initial scaffold: static assets plus /health and /api/catalog. No real offers, storage or cron are implemented yet. The target product exists, but prices and availability remain explicitly unknown. The coding agent is responsible for building and proving the runtime described in PROMPT.md.
# Codex Cloud environment

The repository setup has been tested in a managed cloud workspace. A reusable
environment still needs to be created, saved and published in Codex settings;
this document and `.codex/setup.sh` do not register one automatically.

## Create the environment

In ChatGPT or the Codex desktop app, open Settings → Codex Cloud → Environments →
Create environment. Select `igor-makarov/attention-shoppers-happy-hunting`, use
`main`, and select Get started. Name the environment `Attention shoppers` and keep
Who can use set to Only me.

Ask the setup conversation to install **Node 24.14.0**, matching `mise.toml` and
CI, and ensure it is on PATH in both installation and future task shells. The
setup script checks the version; it does not install Node itself. Keep Wrangler
at the lockfile-pinned version and include development dependencies.

Configure these non-secret environment variables so that later terminal commands
use writable paths too. Exports inside the install script alone do not configure
future task shells.

| Variable | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` | `/workspace/.cache/attention-shoppers/config` |
| `npm_config_cache` | `/workspace/.cache/attention-shoppers/npm` |
| `WRANGLER_SEND_METRICS` | `false` |

Enable internet access and use All (unrestricted) for public vendor research,
which needs to discover sources whose hosts are not known yet. Node installation

No environment secrets, outbound cloud identities or VPN are required. The

development and verification need no Cloudflare account.

## Install script

```sh

```

This installs the locked dependencies with lifecycle scripts disabled, runs the
Worker tests, and builds with `wrangler deploy --dry-run`. Run it again when

outputs remain ignored by Git.

```text
Work in the attention-shoppers-happy-hunting repository checkout.

```

For the older Code Review / GitHub integration environment settings, select Node

# Two owner handoffs

## 1. OpenCode key

Add OPENCODE_API_KEY under repository Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → New repository secret. Paste it only in GitHub's secret form, never into chat, a prompt, a dispatch input or a commit.

The repository variable SHURIK_ENABLED starts false, so scheduled recovery and manual dispatch cannot start a model loop before setup is finished. The owner has added the key and authorized DeepSeek V4.1 Flash on OpenCode Go. After the key is present, the maintainer sets SHURIK_ENABLED true and dispatches:

```sh
gh workflow run shurik.yml --repo igor-makarov/attention-shoppers-happy-hunting --ref main \
  -f command=start -f loop_id=main -f seconds=1800
```

Provider, model and reasoning are fixed in the workflow's control action to opencode-go / deepseek-v4.1-flash / max. Further model changes require an owner instruction and a workflow update. The initial loop writes directly to main. Unless a deadline is supplied it continues until stopped, including after ordinary agent answers. Provider availability and the owner's OpenCode Go allowance apply.

To stop, dispatch command=stop and loop_id=main. Record the durable stop before turning SHURIK_ENABLED false. To resume, use command=resume, loop_id=main; the workflow supplies max reasoning again and updates the saved model to DeepSeek V4.1 Flash. Control/session history and Actions logs are public; do not add private material to this task.

## 2. Cloudflare Git integration

Wait until the maintainer verifies the agent's Ready for Cloudflare handoff status, then stop the coding loop for the owner setup. The owner connects the repo from the Cloudflare dashboard, not through Shurik.

- Workers & Pages → Create application → Import a repository.

- Production branch: main. Root directory: repository root.
- Build command: npm run verify. Confirm the build installs the pinned package-lock.json with npm ci and includes dev dependencies. Use Node 24.14.0 where supported.
- Deploy command: npx --no-install wrangler deploy.
- Disable builds/previews for non-production branches, especially shurik-control/*.
- Keep CF credentials inside Cloudflare. Use a build token scoped only to this Worker and the minimum permissions required for any configured storage. Do not add CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN or CF account secrets to GitHub.

The scaffold currently needs only the ASSETS binding declared in wrangler.jsonc; Wrangler packages the public directory. It has no persistence or scheduled refresh yet. Shurik must update this document with the final bindings, migration/provisioning steps, cron expression and local refresh proof before claiming readiness.

Do not configure a bare deploy command that skips verification. A failed test or dry-run build must prevent production deployment. Validate one actual Shurik-authored main push after connecting CF, then confirm /health, the board and the scheduled refresh in the Cloudflare dashboard. CF Git integration is documented at https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/ci-cd/builds/.

Local checks require no CF account:


The real deployment remains disabled until the owner enables it from Cloudflare. The Actions loop has no direct administrative CF access, but its main code pushes become production changes once automatic deployment is enabled.
# Swiss signage design

The earlier detailed design discussion was not recoverable from the available chat history. This brief records the explicit direction and subsequent owner corrections for this project.

- Use Swiss transport signage as the visual reference: strict alignment, modular grids, numbered sections, clear hierarchy, flat surfaces and strong rules between comparison rows.
- Helvetica/Arial or an equivalent neutral grotesque. Large, tightly composed headings; tabular numerals for ILS totals; comfortable text sizes for conditions and timestamps. Use local/system fonts initially.
- Paper/white backgrounds and near-black type form the neutral structure. Color never decorates an arbitrary heading or vendor.
- Green means verified in-stock availability. Red means out of stock/unavailable. Amber/yellow means pending, uncertain or stale. Always write the status as text; color alone is insufficient. “Best delivered total” should be stated explicitly without a second ambiguous green meaning.
- No emoji in typography. Arrows and wayfinding marks must be monochrome SVG or unambiguous text glyphs that cannot render as colorful emoji. No flags, shopping-cart emoji, coffee emoji or emoji badges.
- Clear rows with consistent columns: vendor, pack/quantity, item price, shipping, delivered total, stock and checked time. At narrow widths reflow each row while preserving the same hierarchy; do not hide shipping conditions.
- Buttons and links require visible keyboard focus. Aim for WCAG AA contrast. Support RTL fragments and Hebrew vendor/product text with correct directionality.
- Prefer factual shopping copy. Distinguish checked data, inferred estimates, stale observations and unknowns. Avoid fake success counters and invented prices.

Stage: Scaffold; not ready for Cloudflare handoff.

# Attention shoppers. Happy hunting.

Build a public, self-updating website on Cloudflare Workers that finds ways to order products online for delivery in Israel and compares the item price plus shipping. Start with Lavazza Crema e Gusto vacuum-packed ground coffee, then make it straightforward to add other products and vendors. This is a working shopping tool, not a marketing landing page.

The owner chose Shurik v1 and explicitly switched the coding loop to opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash at its maximum supported reasoning, max, after repeated Step 5 endpoint errors. Use concrete milestones, short feedback cycles and verifiable evidence. This specific model switch is authorized; do not change provider/model or add another fallback without the owner's instruction. If the provider becomes unavailable, record the issue for the maintainer.

The coding loop writes directly to main. After the owner connects Cloudflare Workers Builds, main pushes will auto-deploy. Shurik has no Cloudflare credentials, API access or deployment tools. All development and integration validation must work locally. Read AGENTS.md and the design/architecture docs.

## Required shopping behavior

1. Discover and validate several actual vendor listings. Use public vendor APIs or public product pages and permitted structured data. Record source URLs, retrieval dates and what each source establishes. Prefer vendors serving Israel; international vendors qualify only when delivery to Israel is evidenced.
2. Match the actual product: Lavazza, Crema e Gusto, ground coffee in a vacuum brick. Record grams, pack count and blend variant. Do not confuse beans, capsules, pods or similarly named products. Classico, Forte and other variants must remain separate. A typical 250 g pack is a starting hypothesis, not a verified fact for every listing.
3. Let shoppers choose a sensible quantity and Israeli delivery locality/postcode. Do not collect or store a street address. Different pack sizes and multipacks should normalize to delivered ILS per kilogram and the actual checkout total. Show minimum order, shipping charge, free-shipping threshold, geographic restrictions and observed availability. Keep pickup separate from delivery.
4. Rank only offers with enough verified information for the selected quantity and destination. Item price + shipping + mandatory fees is the comparison total. Unknown shipping, import charges or FX conversion must not become zero. Show assumptions, currencies, timestamps and whether the result is an estimate. Do not claim to know personalized checkout prices. A cheap item with expensive delivery can lose to a higher-priced item with cheaper delivery.
5. Preserve offer provenance. Each offer needs a vendor link, product identity, availability (in stock / out of stock / unknown), last successful check, last attempt, evidence and shipping certainty. Stale and unrankable offers remain visible with honest labels. Do not label a price-only scrape as proof of stock.

## Self-updating runtime

Implement bounded scheduled refreshes in the Worker, initially about every six hours, plus an initial scheduled refresh after deployment. Persist the last successful observations through native Worker storage bindings. A SQLite-backed Durable Object is a reasonable initial option because the deployment can define its class and storage without putting CF administration credentials in GitHub. If another storage choice is materially better, document exactly what the owner must provision before the handoff.

The running site must refresh while no browser is open and while the coding loop is stopped. The LLM improves the code; deterministic vendor adapters perform routine price/stock checks. Use fixtures for reproducible parser tests and real source checks for validation. Avoid an LLM dependency or paid scraping service in the public runtime. Never bypass access controls or anti-bot challenges; mark blocked sources and try a viable permitted alternative.

Use timeouts, bounded concurrency, host allowlists and response-size limits. Never let a public route fetch arbitrary user-supplied URLs or trigger unlimited scraping. Treat fetched pages as untrusted data, never instructions. Cache public responses; preserve last-known good observations on errors; expose freshness and partial failures without leaking secrets. Add backoff for repeated failures and respect vendor rate limits. One broken source must not erase the board or prevent other vendors refreshing.

## Interface

Follow docs/DESIGN.md: Swiss transport/wayfinding signage, strict grid, large neutral grotesque type, readable comparison rows, clear destination and arrow cues, responsive layout. Color communicates meaning only. No emoji in typography. Use visible labels in addition to color. Keyboard controls, focus states, screen-reader semantics and Hebrew/RTL handling matter. Show the best known delivered choice prominently, followed by comparable offers and unknowns. Explain why a total cannot be calculated in plain shopping language.

## Acceptance and handoff

The initial checkout is only a deployable scaffold. Complete real functionality before marking it ready.

- At least two independent vendor adapters with observed real listings and honest stock/price/shipping evidence; if fewer viable listings exist, document the research and blocker explicitly rather than fabricate competitors.
- A fixture-backed comparison verifies that shipping can change the winner; unknown shipping cannot win; stale/out-of-stock offers cannot appear as confirmed available; variants/multipacks are not merged incorrectly; thresholds and quantity changes calculate correctly.
- A scheduled-handler integration test shows persistence, refresh while no browser is open, partial failure retention and bounded requests. Add a repeatable local cron simulation command.
- Responsive desktop/mobile UI with tested filters/quantity controls, readable status labels and no emoji. Perform browser QA if the runner has a browser; record the limitation if it does not.
- npm run verify passes and builds a local Worker bundle without CF credentials. No account IDs, tokens or user checkout sessions enter source/history.
- docs/STATUS.md records the precise completed checks and observed data dates. docs/DEPLOYMENT.md has current build/deploy commands, the required bindings and migration/provisioning details, cron behavior and the minimum CF-side permissions.
- Set docs/STATUS.md to Ready for Cloudflare handoff and list any remaining owner steps. Never deploy or connect Cloudflare yourself. Continue useful local verification and repair; the maintainer controls stopping/resuming the outer Shurik loop.

Keep progress across iterations using repository docs and Shurik's history tools. Choose the next small, useful task, verify it, and leave a clear next step. Avoid rewriting working components just to change frameworks.

# Architecture and authority

There are two independent loops:

1. Shurik on GitHub Actions develops and checkpoints source to main. It uses only OPENCODE_API_KEY and the repository GITHUB_TOKEN. Its state/history is public on shurik-control/main.
2. The deployed Worker refreshes vendor observations using deterministic scheduled adapters, persists them through runtime bindings and serves the public comparison board. It does not need Shurik or an LLM to keep refreshing.

Cloudflare Workers Builds will be connected by the owner after the second handoff. It observes main pushes and performs validation before deploying. No CF deployment workflow or CF API secret belongs in GitHub. Exclude shurik-control/* and all other branches from Cloudflare builds and previews.

This prevents Shurik's Actions process from directly authenticating to CF. It is not a sandbox for agent-authored code: Shurik writes main, so its code and configuration can influence the CF build and live Worker. CF build commands can run source-controlled code in a credentialed environment. Restrict the CF build token to this Worker and the minimum required permissions; avoid broad account permissions or unrelated build/runtime secrets. Prefer runtime bindings over administrative API tokens. Never give the public Worker an administrative CF token.

GitHub normally does not trigger another push workflow for a push using GITHUB_TOKEN. Do not rely on CI being automatically triggered by every Shurik checkpoint. Shurik must run local verification, and Cloudflare's build command must run npm run verify for every deployment. After connecting CF, verify one actual Shurik push reaches Workers Builds; never assume third-party webhook behavior from GitHub Actions behavior alone.

Start with vendor-specific adapters, a shared product/offer schema, a pure quote/ranking module, persistence and the scheduled-handler pipeline. Keep fetching separate from parsing and pricing. Public routes are read-only and use cached snapshots; public shoppers must not be able to initiate unlimited vendor traffic.

# Swiss signage design

The earlier detailed design discussion was not recoverable from the available chat history. This brief records the explicit direction and subsequent owner corrections for this project.

- Use Swiss transport signage as the visual reference: strict alignment, modular grids, numbered sections, clear hierarchy, flat surfaces and strong rules between comparison rows.

- Paper/white backgrounds and near-black type form the neutral structure. Color never decorates an arbitrary heading or vendor.

When the maintainer verifies the agent's Ready for Cloudflare handoff status, stop the coding loop for the owner setup. The owner connects the repo from the Cloudflare dashboard, not through Shurik.

- Workers & Pages → Create application → Import a repository.
- Select igor-makarov/attention-shoppers-happy-hunting.
- Worker name: attention-shoppers-happy-hunting (must match `name` in wrangler.jsonc).
- Production branch: main. Root directory: repository root.
- Build command: `npm ci --ignore-scripts && npm run verify`. The verify script runs the node:test suite and `wrangler deploy --dry-run --outdir dist`, which builds the Worker bundle locally without any Cloudflare credential. Confirm Node 24.14.0 where supported.
- Deploy command: `npx --no-install wrangler deploy`.
- Disable builds and previews for non-production branches, especially `shurik-control/*`.
- Keep CF credentials inside Cloudflare. No CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN or CF account secret belongs in GitHub.
- Minimum token scope for Workers Builds: Workers Scripts:Edit for this Worker only (the deploy command creates/updates the script and applies the Durable Object migration). No account-wide or unrelated permissions are needed. The runtime needs no administrative credential at all.

## Required bindings and provisioning

`wrangler.jsonc` declares everything; the owner needs no manual dashboard resource creation:

| Binding | Type | Provisioning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `env.BOARD` | Durable Object, class `BoardStore`, SQLite-backed | Created by migration tag `v1` (`new_sqlite_classes: ["BoardStore"]`) during `wrangler deploy` |
| `env.ASSETS` | Static assets from `public/` | Packaged from the repository |

Nothing else is required: the Worker persists observations, vendor refresh state, FX rates and run history in the Durable Object's SQLite tables (`observations`, `vendor_state`, `meta`, `runs`, plus a `leases` table) and reads vendor pages over plain outbound HTTPS.

Alternative storage was considered and rejected: KV or R2 would add a separate consistency problem and still need a migration path for the lease/last-known-good semantics; the SQLite-backed Durable Object is created by the deployment itself with no extra credential.

## Cron behavior

- `wrangler.jsonc` triggers the scheduled handler on `17 */6 * * *` (UTC), about every six hours.
- The first `GET /health` or `GET /api/board` after a deployment starts one initial refresh in the background so the board is not empty until the first cron tick. It is lease- and throttle-protected (10 minutes) and can never be triggered repeatedly by public traffic.
- Each run fetches at most one URL per tracked offer plus the Bank of Israel rate file, capped at two vendors concurrently, 12 s per request and 1.5 MB per response, with hosts restricted to each adapter's allowlist.
- Failures keep the previous good observation, back off (30 min doubling to 12 h) and are surfaced in `/api/status` and the board footer. One broken vendor cannot stop the others.

## Local verification without a Cloudflare account

```sh
npm ci --ignore-scripts
npm run verify          # node:test suite + wrangler deploy --dry-run
npm run check:sources   # live fetch + parse of every tracked vendor page
npm run cron:offline    # full refresh pipeline against recorded fixtures
npm run cron:local      # full refresh pipeline against the live vendor pages
npm run dev             # local Worker with a local SQLite Durable Object
```

With `npm run dev` running on port 8789, the same commands used during development are:

```sh
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8789/api/board?grams=500\&dest=tel-aviv
curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8789/cdn-cgi/local/scheduled   # simulate the cron trigger
npm run qa:browser http://127.0.0.1:8789                        # headless Chrome desktop+mobile QA
```

The real deployment remains disabled until the owner enables it from Cloudflare. The Actions loop has no direct administrative CF access, but its main code pushes become production changes once automatic deployment is enabled.

# Project status

Stage: **Ready for Cloudflare handoff.** The Worker implements the real self-updating board; the owner
still has to connect Cloudflare Workers Builds (steps at the end of this file and in docs/DEPLOYMENT.md).
No Cloudflare deployment, credential or remote resource was created by the coding loop.

## What the deployed Worker does

- **Comparison board** (`/`, `/api/board`): ranks delivered offers for Lavazza Crema e Gusto vacuum-packed
  ground coffee by item price + shipping + mandatory fees in ILS, normalized to delivered ILS/kg and to
  the packs a shopper actually buys. Destination (six Israeli locality/postcode areas), target grams and
  variant are selectable; no street address is collected.
- **Honest unknowns**: unknown shipping, unknown FX, unknown availability, stale observations and
  out-of-stock offers remain visible with plain-language reasons. Missing data never becomes zero and
  never wins. Pickup is shown separately and never competes with delivery.
- **Provenance**: every offer keeps its vendor link, product identity (variant, form, pack grams, pack
  count, SKU/GTIN), availability with its structured-data evidence URL, last successful check, last
  attempt, parser version and shipping certainty.
- **Self-updating runtime**: `wrangler.jsonc` triggers `17 */6 * * *` (about every six hours); the first
  `/health` or `/api/board` after deployment starts one throttled initial refresh. Observations, vendor
  state, FX rates, run history and leases persist in the SQLite-backed `BoardStore` Durable Object.
- **Bounded fetching**: host allowlists per adapter, 12 s timeout, 1.5 MB response cap, max two vendors
  in flight, one attempt per offer per run, 30 min→12 h backoff per vendor. Public routes never fetch a
  visitor-supplied URL and never start unbounded scraping. Responses are cacheable
  (`public, max-age=300, stale-while-revalidate=3600`) and freshness/partial failures are exposed in the
  API and the board footer.
- **No LLM or paid scraper in the public runtime**: only deterministic adapters, official Bank of Israel
  rates and native Cloudflare storage.

## Live observations (recorded evidence)

Retrieved 2026-10-12 with `npm run check:sources` (bounded fetcher + production parsers) and stored under
`.shurik-local/sources/`. Full source record: docs/SOURCES.md.

| Vendor | Listing | Price | Stock | Shipping | Certainty |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CoffeeMan (IL) | Lavazza Crema e Gusto Classico 250 g ground, SKU 930333 | ₪33 (regular ₪36) | in stock (schema.org microdata) | ₪25 courier; free self-pickup | verified |
| Pucks (IL) | Lavazza Crema e Gusto Classico 250 g ground, SKU Lav69, GTIN 8000070038769 | ₪30.00 | in stock (JSON-LD) | calculated at checkout | unknown (unranked) |

Live board at 500 g to Tel Aviv: best delivered total ₪91.00 = 2 × ₪33 + ₪25 shipping for CoffeeMan
(₪182.00/kg); Pucks is visible as unranked with the reason "shipping is not published before checkout,
so it is treated as unknown, not free". FX reference table from the Bank of Israel dated 2026-10-09.

## Verification performed (2026-10-12, all local)

1. `npm ci --ignore-scripts` — clean install from the pinned lockfile, 0 vulnerabilities.
2. `npm run verify` — 37/37 `node:test` cases pass, then `wrangler deploy --dry-run` builds the Worker
   bundle with no Cloudflare credential (54.60 KiB, gzip 14.89 KiB; bindings `BOARD` + `ASSETS` shown).
   Covered acceptance cases include: shipping changes the winner; unknown shipping cannot win;
   stale/out-of-stock/unknown availability stay unranked; variants and multipacks stay separate;
   quantity rounding, minimum order and free-shipping thresholds; missing FX is not zero; destination
   coverage; pickup separated; leases; backoff; allowlist.
3. `npm run check:sources` (live) — CoffeeMan and Pucks both PASS against the real pages at
   11:04 UTC and 11:20 UTC.
4. `npm run cron:offline` — full refresh pipeline against recorded Windows-1255/JSON-LD fixtures, both
   offers and the FX table persisted.
5. `npm run cron:local` — live pipeline: both vendors refreshed, Bank of Israel rates fetched (USD 3.055).
6. Local Worker runtime (`npx wrangler dev --persist-to ...`, SQLite Durable Object, fresh storage, no
   browser opened): triggering only `/cdn-cgi/local/scheduled` at 11:20 UTC produced a scheduled run with
   3 bounded requests, both vendors saved, `nextAttemptAt` +6 h, and persisted `lastRefreshAt`. A second
   scheduled trigger made 0 requests and skipped both vendors on backoff. `/api/board` then served the
   ranked board from storage. This is the refresh-while-no-browser-open path.
7. `npm run qa:browser` — headless Chrome (chromedriver 154) QA: **23/23 checks pass**, exit 0, desktop
   1440 px and mobile 390 px, screenshots and JSON report in `.shurik-local/qa/`. Checks include:
   best delivered total and per-kg math, written stock labels, unknown-shipping reason, destination and
   quantity controls, shareable URL updates, keyboard Tab focus with a visible 3 px focus outline and
   Enter activation, Hebrew text isolated with `dir="auto"`, no emoji anywhere in the visible text, no
   horizontal overflow, and 44 px touch targets on mobile.

This iteration (3-49) fixed three real defects found by the new QA: quantity buttons were dead because
`el()` registered `addEventListener('Click')` instead of `click`; the browser QA harness misread the
W3C element id, never polled page conditions (`waitFor` misuse) and deleted the wrong session path; and
Hebrew vendor/product names were not direction-isolated. Added `npm run check:sources` and
`npm run qa:browser` for repeatable evidence.

## Repository and security checks

- No account IDs, API tokens, checkout sessions or addresses in source, docs or history (secret scan run).
- `wrangler.jsonc` defines the Durable Object class and migration, so no manual CF provisioning is
  needed and no administrative credential lives in GitHub.
- Research blockers recorded honestly in docs/SOURCES.md: rami-levy.co.il returns 403 (anti-bot, not
  bypassed); tivtaam.co.il is a JS-only SPA; amazon.com has no public evidence of delivery to Israel for
  the tracked listing, so it is excluded rather than guessed.

## Remaining owner steps (Cloudflare handoff)

1. Stop the coding loop for the setup window (maintainer action; see docs/DEPLOYMENT.md handoff 1).
2. In Cloudflare: Workers & Pages → Create application → Import a repository → select
   igor-makarov/attention-shoppers-happy-hunting. Worker name `attention-shoppers-happy-hunting`.
3. Production branch `main`; build command `npm ci --ignore-scripts && npm run verify`; deploy command
   `npx --no-install wrangler deploy`; Node 24.x.
4. Disable builds/previews for every other branch, especially `shurik-control/*`.
5. Use the minimum build credential (Workers Scripts:Edit for this Worker only). Never add a CF token to
   GitHub or to the Worker.
6. After the first deploy, confirm `/health` reports `lastRefreshAt`, the board shows the two observed
   offers, and the 6-hour cron trigger is listed. Then verify that one later main push is picked up by
   Workers Builds.
7. If anything fails, report the Cloudflare error back to the loop; do not paste credentials.

## Loop notes

- Model/provider: opencode-go / deepseek-v4.1-flash at max reasoning (owner-authorized). Iterations
  2-45…2-47 hit provider 429 "Endpoint is unavailable" before any work landed; session 3-48 timed out
  mid vendor research, but its checkpoints are preserved. This iteration ran normally.
- Next useful task for the loop: add a third vendor adapter only with evidenced Israeli delivery, keep
  `npm run check:sources` green against live pages, and re-run `npm run qa:browser` after UI changes.

A public online shopping board for delivery in Israel, starting with **Lavazza Crema e Gusto vacuum-packed ground coffee**. The goal is to compare actual availability and item price plus shipping for a selected quantity and destination, with visible source evidence and freshness.

Swiss signage design, meaningful status colors, no emoji typography. Unknown shipping is never silently treated as free.

This initial commit is a deployable scaffold, not a completed price tracker. Shurik builds the remaining functionality from [PROMPT.md](PROMPT.md). See [current status](docs/STATUS.md), [design](docs/DESIGN.md) and [architecture](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md).

## Coding loop

The workflow uses [igor-makarov/shurik@v1](https://github.com/igor-makarov/shurik), opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash and max reasoning. The owner chose direct work on main and has added the OPENCODE_API_KEY Actions secret. The first handoff is complete; the main loop will develop the tracker while Cloudflare remains disconnected. Check the Actions page and shurik-control/main for live loop state.

DeepSeek V4.1 Flash is present in Shurik's pinned Pi AI catalog and supports low, high and max reasoning. Its native adapter preserves reasoning content across tool calls. The owner authorized this switch after Step 5 returned repeated unavailable-endpoint errors. No further model fallback is permitted without an owner instruction.

## Deployment and refreshing

The owner will enable auto-deploy on main pushes from **Cloudflare Workers Builds** at the second handoff. GitHub stores no CF credentials and has no deployment job. Once implemented, Worker Cron Triggers and native runtime storage will refresh the offer board independently of the coding loop.

Follow [the two handoffs](docs/DEPLOYMENT.md). Agent-authored code can affect the CF build and production Worker once auto-deploy is enabled; keeping CF API credentials out of Shurik does not remove that authority.

## Develop locally

Node 24.14.0, pinned dependencies:

```sh
npm ci --ignore-scripts
npm run verify
npm run dev
```

The verification build is Wrangler deploy --dry-run and does not publish to Cloudflare.

For a reusable Codex workspace, follow the [Codex Cloud setup](docs/CODEX_CLOUD.md).

Iteration 3-49 is complete, verified, and committed with a clean working tree.

## What this iteration found and fixed

The repo already had a substantial implementation from the interrupted 3-48 session (adapters, quote engine, refresh pipeline, SQLite Durable Object store, UI, 37 tests). I verified it end-to-end and fixed three real defects that the acceptance checks depended on:

1. **Dead quantity controls** — `public/app.js` registered `addEventListener('Click')` instead of `click`, so the 250 g–2 kg buttons did nothing in a browser. Fixed to lowercase the event name.
2. **Browser QA harness broken** — it read the legacy `ELEMENT` key instead of the W3C element id, misused `waitFor` so page-event polling never ran, deleted the wrong session path, and could leave the runner waiting on child processes. Fixed, plus added state probes on timeout.
3. **Missing Hebrew/RTL isolation** — the `hebrew()` helper was dead code; Hebrew vendor/product names now render in `dir="auto"` isolated spans, with a QA check.

## Verified evidence (2026-10-12, all local, no CF credentials)

- `npm run verify`: **37/37 tests pass** + Wrangler 4.149.0 `deploy --dry-run` bundle (54.60 KiB / 14.89 KiB gzip).
- `npm run check:sources` (new): live PASS for both adapters — CoffeeMan ₪33, 250 g Classico, in stock, ₪25 courier + free pickup; Pucks ₪30, 250 g Classico, in stock, shipping unknown → unranked.
- Fresh-state Wrangler dev run, **no browser opened**: triggering only `/cdn-cgi/local/scheduled` produced 3 bounded requests, both vendors saved, FX fetched, `nextAttemptAt` +6 h persisted; a second trigger made 0 requests (backoff). Board served ₪91.00 delivered for 500 g to Tel Aviv.
- `npm run qa:browser` (new): **23/23 checks pass**, exit 0 — desktop 1440 px + mobile 390 px, keyboard Tab/Enter with visible focus outline, quantity/destination/URL updates, written stock labels, unknown-shipping reason, no emoji, Hebrew `dir="auto"`, no horizontal overflow, 44 px touch targets.
- Edge cases: quantity clamping, unknown destination/variant/product, 404/405 routes all behave honestly.
- Secret scan clean; no dev processes left running.

## Docs set to handoff

- `docs/STATUS.md` → **Ready for Cloudflare handoff**, with exact checks, timestamps and remaining owner steps.
- `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md` → bindings (`BOARD` Durable Object migration + `ASSETS`), cron `17 */6 * * *`, build/deploy commands, minimum CF permissions, local verification commands.
- `docs/SOURCES.md` → source URLs, retrieval dates, what each source establishes, and honest blockers (Rami Levy 403, Tivtaam JS-only SPA, Amazon lacks evidenced IL delivery; eBay/iHerb blocked — not bypassed).
- `docs/evidence/` → committed snapshots of the source check, scheduled runtime proof and 23 QA checks.

**Nothing was deployed or connected to Cloudflare.** The owner still needs to connect Workers Builds (steps in DEPLOYMENT.md). Provider note for the maintainer: iterations 2-45…2-47 failed with 429 endpoint errors; this iteration ran normally on DeepSeek V4.1 Flash.

# Attention shoppers. Happy hunting.

Build a public, self-updating website on Cloudflare Workers that finds ways to order products online for delivery in Israel and compares the item price plus shipping. Start with Lavazza Crema e Gusto vacuum-packed ground coffee, then make it straightforward to add other products and vendors. This is a working shopping tool, not a marketing landing page.

The owner chose Shurik v1 and explicitly switched the coding loop to opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash at its maximum supported reasoning, max, after repeated Step 5 endpoint errors. Use concrete milestones, short feedback cycles and verifiable evidence. This specific model switch is authorized; do not change provider/model or add another fallback without the owner's instruction. If the provider becomes unavailable, record the issue for the maintainer.

The coding loop writes directly to main. After the owner connects Cloudflare Workers Builds, main pushes will auto-deploy. Shurik has no Cloudflare credentials, API access or deployment tools. All development and integration validation must work locally. Read AGENTS.md and the design/architecture docs.

## Required shopping behavior

1. Discover and validate several actual vendor listings. Use public vendor APIs or public product pages and permitted structured data. Record source URLs, retrieval dates and what each source establishes. Prefer vendors serving Israel; international vendors qualify only when delivery to Israel is evidenced.
2. Match the actual product: Lavazza, Crema e Gusto, ground coffee in a vacuum brick. Record grams, pack count and blend variant. Do not confuse beans, capsules, pods or similarly named products. Classico, Forte and other variants must remain separate. A typical 250 g pack is a starting hypothesis, not a verified fact for every listing.
3. Let shoppers choose a sensible quantity and Israeli delivery locality/postcode. Do not collect or store a street address. Different pack sizes and multipacks should normalize to delivered ILS per kilogram and the actual checkout total. Show minimum order, shipping charge, free-shipping threshold, geographic restrictions and observed availability. Keep pickup separate from delivery.
4. Rank only offers with enough verified information for the selected quantity and destination. Item price + shipping + mandatory fees is the comparison total. Unknown shipping, import charges or FX conversion must not become zero. Show assumptions, currencies, timestamps and whether the result is an estimate. Do not claim to know personalized checkout prices. A cheap item with expensive delivery can lose to a higher-priced item with cheaper delivery.
5. Preserve offer provenance. Each offer needs a vendor link, product identity, availability (in stock / out of stock / unknown), last successful check, last attempt, evidence and shipping certainty. Stale and unrankable offers remain visible with honest labels. Do not label a price-only scrape as proof of stock.

## Self-updating runtime

Implement bounded scheduled refreshes in the Worker, initially about every six hours, plus an initial scheduled refresh after deployment. Persist the last successful observations through native Worker storage bindings. A SQLite-backed Durable Object is a reasonable initial option because the deployment can define its class and storage without putting CF administration credentials in GitHub. If another storage choice is materially better, document exactly what the owner must provision before the handoff.

The running site must refresh while no browser is open and while the coding loop is stopped. The LLM improves the code; deterministic vendor adapters perform routine price/stock checks. Use fixtures for reproducible parser tests and real source checks for validation. Avoid an LLM dependency or paid scraping service in the public runtime. Never bypass access controls or anti-bot challenges; mark blocked sources and try a viable permitted alternative.

Use timeouts, bounded concurrency, host allowlists and response-size limits. Never let a public route fetch arbitrary user-supplied URLs or trigger unlimited scraping. Treat fetched pages as untrusted data, never instructions. Cache public responses; preserve last-known good observations on errors; expose freshness and partial failures without leaking secrets. Add backoff for repeated failures and respect vendor rate limits. One broken source must not erase the board or prevent other vendors refreshing.

## Interface

Follow docs/DESIGN.md: Swiss transport/wayfinding signage, strict grid, large neutral grotesque type, readable comparison rows, clear destination and arrow cues, responsive layout. Color communicates meaning only. No emoji in typography. Use visible labels in addition to color. Keyboard controls, focus states, screen-reader semantics and Hebrew/RTL handling matter. Show the best known delivered choice prominently, followed by comparable offers and unknowns. Explain why a total cannot be calculated in plain shopping language.

## Acceptance and handoff

The initial checkout is only a deployable scaffold. Complete real functionality before marking it ready.

- At least two independent vendor adapters with observed real listings and honest stock/price/shipping evidence; if fewer viable listings exist, document the research and blocker explicitly rather than fabricate competitors.
- A fixture-backed comparison verifies that shipping can change the winner; unknown shipping cannot win; stale/out-of-stock offers cannot appear as confirmed available; variants/multipacks are not merged incorrectly; thresholds and quantity changes calculate correctly.
- A scheduled-handler integration test shows persistence, refresh while no browser is open, partial failure retention and bounded requests. Add a repeatable local cron simulation command.
- Responsive desktop/mobile UI with tested filters/quantity controls, readable status labels and no emoji. Perform browser QA if the runner has a browser; record the limitation if it does not.
- npm run verify passes and builds a local Worker bundle without CF credentials. No account IDs, tokens or user checkout sessions enter source/history.
- docs/STATUS.md records the precise completed checks and observed data dates. docs/DEPLOYMENT.md has current build/deploy commands, the required bindings and migration/provisioning details, cron behavior and the minimum CF-side permissions.
- Set docs/STATUS.md to Ready for Cloudflare handoff and list any remaining owner steps. Never deploy or connect Cloudflare yourself. Continue useful local verification and repair; the maintainer controls stopping/resuming the outer Shurik loop.

Keep progress across iterations using repository docs and Shurik's history tools. Choose the next small, useful task, verify it, and leave a clear next step. Avoid rewriting working components just to change frameworks.
